diagnosis.summary: product-service is experiencing severe Lambda handler slowness, with mean handler execution time and end-to-end latency both roughly 300x above baseline. payment-service shows a roughly 2.3x rise in request rate while its handler duration and end-to-end latency remain near baseline. No 5xx errors are recorded on either service.
diagnosis.root_cause: Severe Lambda handler degradation in product-service, where handler CPU time rose approximately 306x above baseline, is the most likely root cause.
evidence: product-service lambda_duration_ms_mean rose from 2.486 ms to 759.65 ms, a ~306x increase, and lambda_duration_ms_p95 rose from 3.12 ms to 761.59 ms, a ~244x increase.
product-service end-to-end latency rose sharply across all measured percentiles: p50 from 4.09 ms to 893.32 ms (~218x), p95 from 6.56 ms to 903.5 ms (~138x), and p99 from 9.59 ms to 906.04 ms (~94x).

The magnitude of the product-service latency rise at each percentile closely matches the rise in lambda_duration_ms at the corresponding percentile (mean handler time 759.65 ms, p50 latency 893.32 ms; p95 handler time 761.59 ms, p95 latency 903.5 ms).

payment-service request_rate rose from 0.94 rps to 2.15 rps (~2.3x), while its lambda_duration_ms_mean fell slightly from 0.5855 ms to 0.3012 ms and p95_latency_ms held near baseline at 4.43 ms versus 4.51 ms.
error_rate_5xx remains at 0 on both product-service and payment-service.
recommended_actions: Inspect CloudWatch Logs for /aws/lambda/anomalypulse-product for slow code paths or unexpected computation active during this window.
Check the CloudWatch Errors metric for anomalypulse-product to identify any invocations cut off by the timeout, which would not appear in error_rate_5xx or the latency percentiles.

Review any recent changes to the anomalypulse-product function code, layers, or configuration that could account for the ~306x increase in handler execution time, and roll back only if logs confirm the slow path is in code that change touched.
After identifying and addressing the slow code path, recheck lambda_duration_ms_mean and p95_latency_ms for product-service to confirm recovery.
Investigate the payment-service request rate increase in parallel to determine whether it reflects a separate workload shift.
